facts.text: McCaskill got its name in 1912 when the post office, originally called Dixon, was renamed after Daniel Berryman McCaskill, a local agricultural pioneer.
The town sprang to life around 1900 when the Prescott and Northwestern Railroad arrived, turning a quiet outpost into a lumber and crop shipping hub.
McCaskill sits on flat to gently rolling blackland prairie, where fertile soils once made the area both productive and remote before roads improved access.
Spring and summer in McCaskill bring frequent thunderstorms as warm, moist Gulf air rises, creating high humidity that peaks from May through September.
The average annual temperature hovers around 62°F, with July and August highs reaching 93°F and January lows dipping to about 31°F.
McCaskill receives roughly 54 inches of rain each year, most of it falling in spring—May alone sees about 5.6 inches of precipitation.
